content: Like an eye that sees everything except itself, the healthy human soul looks outward toward reality.
author: Viktor Frankl
sourceWork: Yes to Life: In Spite of Everything (1946)
story:
Rather than offering a polite platitude, this observation challenges how we navigate our inner lives. True wisdom is rarely complicated or flashy, but it demands the honesty to look at our own habits and assumptions without defensive excuses.

In Viktor Frankl's view, genuine strength is not an abstract theory—it is a lived, daily practice. When you stop looking for external validation and anchor your self-worth in quiet integrity, the noisy chaos of the world loses its power over you. A good life is built day by day through small, conscious choices.
reflectionPrompt: How can acknowledging your vulnerability help you build deeper self-trust and inner peace?
